themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Surge in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.4 per week (967% increase, z-score 5.21), suggesting either a recent weather event, disease outbreak, or maintenance failure affecting Williamsbridge/Baychester green spaces.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike)
Z-score of 5.21 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community Board has standing budget request for 'new equipment for maintenance' to Parks and Recreation, suggesting chronic tree care gaps
reporting_angles: Are specific parks affected? Interview Parks Dept. about tree health assessments and maintenance schedules.
Did recent weather (cold snap, heavy rain) trigger decline? Cross-reference with meteorological data.

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Crisis Explodes
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests exploded to 3 complaints LAST WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week (2300% surge, z-score 8.69—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset), indicating severe sanitation infrastructure failure or rapid deterioration.
evidence: 3 litter basket complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, highest z-score: 8.69)
Concurrent with 909 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (endemic sanitation problem)
Suggests either broken baskets not being replaced or inadequate basket distribution across district
reporting_angles: Map where baskets are missing or broken—are certain neighborhoods (parks, commercial strips) disproportionately affected?
Interview Sanitation Department about maintenance and replacement timelines; check if budget cuts affected basket servicing.

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints surged 5x baseline (3 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average, z-score 5.0) over the PAST 2 WEEKS, signaling either a sudden influx of illegal vendors or ramped-up resident complaints about street commerce.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% increase, z-score 5.0)
No corresponding Reddit or news coverage, suggesting dormant issue now surfacing
Community Board budget requests don't explicitly mention street vending, but related to 'roadway maintenance' and 'land use/zoning study'
reporting_angles: Where are illegal vendors concentrated? Interview residents and local business owners about impact on street conditions and safety.
Is NYPD or DOE Sidewalk Vending Unit ramping up enforcement, or are residents newly reporting established vendors?

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis Persists
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dominate the 90-day dataset at 5,691 complaints (second-highest volume), representing a chronic housing code compliance failure affecting thousands of residents during winter months.
evidence: 5,691 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (second-largest complaint category, nearly tied with noise at 5,750)
No spike data provided, suggesting sustained endemic problem rather than recent acceleration
Winter season timing indicates seasonal vulnerability; likely affects low-income, older rental stock
reporting_angles: Profile a family experiencing heat loss; connect to landlord enforcement data and HPD violations.
Analyze which blocks/buildings are repeat offenders; cross-reference with DOB permits to identify deferred maintenance.

themes_detail.label: Hazmat & Animal Issues Converge
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked 1100% (3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 baseline) alongside animal-in-park complaints (also +1100%, same timing), suggesting possible environmental contamination or wildlife migration linked to site conditions.
evidence: Hazardous materials complaints: 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Animal-in-park complaints: 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35—identical timing and magnitude)
Community Board standing request for 'animal and pest control including rat and mosquito reduction,' indicating chronic animal/pest issues
Temporal clustering suggests shared root cause (site contamination, habitat change, or land use disruption)
reporting_angles: Investigate what hazmat incidents occurred 3 weeks ago; were they reported to EPA or DEP? Any industrial or construction activity?

Did animals (coyotes, raccoons, rats) increase because of contamination exposure or habitat loss from development? Cross-reference with active ULURP applications (White Plains Road rezoning, Wakefield Village).
